input.command: cat -n src/jira.ts; ls; ls src; grep -rn "getIssue\|timeout\|AbortSignal\|setGlobalDispatcher\|undici" --include=*.ts --include=*.json . | grep -v node_modules | head -40

input.reason: In src/jira.ts:4, getIssue calls `fetch(`${JIRA}/issue/${key}`)` with no options at all: no `signal`, no AbortSignal.timeout, and no AbortController. Its only caller, the `issue` route handler in src/routes.ts:48, awaits it directly and adds no timeout either. The repository sets no global dispatcher or agent timeout anywhere (a grep for timeout, AbortSignal, setGlobalDispatcher and undici finds nothing), and package.json has no HTTP client dependency. So the only limits are Node's built-in undici defaults: about 10s to connect, and about 300s each for headers and for body idle time. A Jira server that accepts the connection but responds slowly or stalls keeps each issue request pending for up to roughly five minutes, possibly longer if it trickles the body. `res.json()` has no bound either. The review's wording "hangs every caller" is a little too strong, because the wait is bounded by undici's defaults and does not block the event loop. The main defect is real, though: the app sets no timeout of its own. searchAssigned (line 10) has the same pattern.

evidence.location: package.json (full file; no HTTP client deps, no timeout config)

input.failure_scenario: Jira at jira.example.com accepts TCP connections but stops responding, for example because it is overloaded or a proxy is holding requests. Every request to the `issue` route (src/routes.ts:48) awaits getIssue's fetch at src/jira.ts:4, which has no abort signal. Each client waits up to about 300 seconds, undici's default headers timeout, before getting an error. Meanwhile the pending requests and their sockets pile up in the server instead of failing fast.
input.severity_reason: This is a reliability risk that only shows up when the Jira dependency is degraded. Node's fetch still enforces default connect, headers and body timeouts of about 10s and 300s, so requests do not hang forever and the event loop is not blocked. That makes it less serious than an outage on a common path.
